context:
Patient: 54M, ECOG 1, with a rapidly enlarging right cervical mass, dysphagia and morning facial fullness; 12.0 cm anterior mediastinal mass with about 50% SVC narrowing, all disease above the diaphragm, LDH 740 rising to 812, uric acid 7.6 to 7.9, LVEF 60%. Node biopsy was signed out as DLBCL NOS (GCB, MYC 80%/BCL2 90% by IHC, Ki-67 95%), but the 9/19 FISH addendum shows MYC and BCL2 rearrangements after R-CHOP x6 had already been planned to start 9/22.
What this case tests: The late FISH addendum changes the diagnosis to double-hit lymphoma (HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements), not DLBCL NOS. | The R-CHOP plan was written before FISH and must be replaced with intensive therapy such as DA-EPOCH-R x6 or a clinical trial. | Disease is stage II bulky (12 cm mediastinal mass, above the diaphragm only), not stage III or IV. | IPI and CNS-IPI are only 1, but double-hit biology drives the risk, so brain MRI, lumbar puncture and CNS prophylaxis are still needed. | Bulky mass, high LDH and rising uric acid need TLS prophylaxis; DA-EPOCH-R needs G-CSF every cycle and its 96-hour infusion goes through the new port.

answer.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (HGBL-DH, 'double-hit' lymphoma), not DLBCL NOS. Excisional biopsy of the right cervical level III lymph node showed a diffuse aggressive B-cell lymphoma with a germinal-center phenotype (CD20+, PAX5+, CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-, CD5-, cyclin D1-, TdT-, EBER-), BCL2 expression about 90%, MYC expression about 80%, and Ki-67 about 95%. FISH confirmed MYC rearrangement with IGH::MYC t(8;14) and BCL2 rearrangement with IGH::BCL2 t(14;18), with no BCL6 rearrangement. The 2026-09-19 pathology addendum supersedes the initial diagnosis of DLBCL, NOS.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage IIA, bulky: right cervical levels II-IV nodal disease plus a 12.0 cm anterior mediastinal mass, all above the diaphragm, with no B symptoms and no FDG-avid disease below the diaphragm, no extranodal organ involvement, and no osseous or marrow uptake on PET/CT. The mediastinal mass is bulky (>10 cm). Staging is not complete until CSF and bone marrow are assessed; if either is involved, the stage becomes IV.
answer.biology: GCB-type aggressive B-cell lymphoma driven by dual MYC and BCL2 rearrangements, t(8;14) and t(14;18), with high MYC and BCL2 protein expression and very high proliferation (Ki-67 95%). This double-hit biology is associated with resistance to R-CHOP and a substantially increased risk of CNS relapse. EBER is negative and BCL6 is not rearranged. No TP53 mutation or gene-expression data are available.
answer.prognosis: IPI 1 (low), age-adjusted IPI 1 (low-intermediate), and CNS-IPI 1 (low). However, the double-hit histology dominates prognosis and confers high-risk, aggressive behavior. Historical outcomes with R-CHOP were poor, whereas intensive first-line therapy such as DA-EPOCH-R offers the best chance of durable remission. I would describe the disease as potentially curable but high-risk, with a meaningful relapse risk; I would not quote a precise cure probability until CSF and marrow staging and the response to therapy are known.
answer.first_line_treatment: I am cancelling the planned R-CHOP and starting curative-intent DA-EPOCH-R (dose-adjusted etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, plus rituximab) for 6 cycles at 21-day intervals, with G-CSF and dose adjustment based on nadir ANC and platelets. R-CHOP is inadequate for HGBL-DH; DA-EPOCH-R is the NCCN-preferred standard regimen for this histology, with a clinical trial preferred if one is available. Cycle 1 should start as soon as CSF and marrow staging and tumor-lysis precautions are addressed; I would not delay treatment for the full 6-cycle plan. If he cannot tolerate intensive therapy, I would use a dose-modified intensive regimen rather than R-CHOP, but he is currently fit.
answer.cns_risk: The CNS-IPI is 1 (low: elevated LDH only; age <60, ECOG 1, stage II, no more than one extranodal site, and no kidney or adrenal involvement), but double-hit histology is an independent high-risk feature and the CNS-IPI underestimates CNS risk in HGBL-DH. I will perform a lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry before cycle 1. If the CSF is negative, I will give CNS prophylaxis with intrathecal methotrexate 12 mg for 4 doses starting with cycle 2, with attention to thrombocytopenia and neurotoxicity. If the CSF is positive, I will treat CNS disease with a high-dose methotrexate-based approach rather than intrathecal therapy alone. The benefit of prophylaxis in this setting is not proven, so this remains a judgment call.
answer.response_assessment: Baseline PET/CT is available. I will reassess with PET/CT after cycle 2 for interim response and prognosis, and again 6-8 weeks after cycle 6 using Lugano/Deauville criteria. Deauville 1-3 at end of treatment is complete metabolic response; Deauville 4-5 is non-response or persistent disease and should be biopsy-confirmed if feasible. I will not change therapy solely on an interim Deauville 4 outside a trial, but unequivocal progression or a positive interim scan would prompt early salvage. If end-of-treatment disease persists, I would use platinum-based salvage such as R-ICE or R-DHAP and consolidate with autologous HCT if chemosensitive; relapsed or refractory disease would be considered for CAR-T therapy.
answer.pretreatment_workup: Completed: excisional biopsy with IHC and FISH, contrast CT of the neck and chest, FDG PET/CT, baseline echocardiogram (LVEF 60%), CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH, uric acid, beta-2 microglobulin, hepatitis B/C and HIV serologies, and port placement. Before cycle 1 I will complete: lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry; bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (PET-negative marrow does not fully exclude involvement, and HGBL often involves marrow); G6PD testing before any rasburicase; fertility counseling and sperm banking; review of the amended pathology by hematopathology; and formal documentation of Ann Arbor stage, IPI, and CNS-IPI. Hepatitis B: HBsAg negative, anti-HBc negative, anti-HBs positive (immune), so no antiviral prophylaxis is needed. HCV and HIV are negative. I will also confirm dental evaluation and update inactivated vaccinations before rituximab if feasible.
answer.supportive_care: He is at high risk for tumor lysis because of bulky disease, LDH more than 3 times the upper limit of normal, and uric acid 7.9. Start allopurinol 300 mg daily and aggressive hydration now, check G6PD, and give rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg before cycle 1 if G6PD is normal, with frequent potassium, calcium, phosphorus, creatinine, and uric acid monitoring around cycle 1. DA-EPOCH-R requires pegfilgrastim 6 mg on day 6, or filgrastim, with nadir-based dose adjustment. Give NK1/5-HT3/dexamethasone antiemetics, a bowel regimen for vincristine, and monitor for neuropathy. Continue CPAP for OSA and omeprazole for GERD. No routine PJP or antibacterial prophylaxis unless he has prolonged steroids or neutropenia; no live vaccines during rituximab; update influenza, COVID, and pneumococcal vaccines. HBV reactivation risk is low given anti-HBc negativity. Monitor for SVC syndrome and airway compromise, with head-of-bed elevation and urgent evaluation for stridor or worsening facial swelling, and monitor for anthracycline cardiotoxicity (cumulative doxorubicin about 240 mg/m2; repeat echocardiogram if symptoms). Offer sperm banking before cycle 1 and provide psychosocial and financial support.
answer.fitness_and_goals: He is fit for intensive curative therapy: age 54, ECOG 1, working, LVEF 60%, normal renal and hepatic function, controlled OSA, mild asthma, and GERD, BMI 30.2, no prior cancer therapy, and good social support with a wife at home and a residence 20 minutes from the cancer center. He explicitly wants the treatment with the best chance of cure and hopes to keep working part-time; the 96-hour infusion and frequent visits of DA-EPOCH-R are feasible with his support and proximity. I will maintain dose intensity with G-CSF and nadir-based adjustment rather than elective dose reduction. If his performance status declines or toxicity becomes prohibitive, I would modify the regimen and revisit goals; at present, the goal is cure.
missing_information: CSF cytology and flow cytometry by lumbar puncture have not been performed; CNS staging is incomplete.
Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy have not been documented; Ann Arbor stage may change to IV if involved.
G6PD status is unknown, which is needed before rasburicase.
Fertility preservation and sperm banking have not been documented.
No formal Ann Arbor stage, IPI, or CNS-IPI is documented in the chart; these were calculated here from available data.
No TP53 mutation or gene-expression/cell-of-origin data are available; these are not required for the immediate decision but may inform prognosis.
No baseline dental evaluation is documented before anthracycline-based chemotherapy.

items.criterion: The response revises the diagnosis to high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit; WHO-HAEM5 DLBCL/HGBL-MYC/BCL2 also accepted) based on the 2026-09-19 FISH addendum, rather than keeping the original DLBCL NOS sign-out.
The response keeps the final diagnosis as DLBCL NOS (or otherwise denies that this is double-hit / HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements).
The response notes a germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-).
The response recognizes that the 2026-09-14 plan (R-CHOP x6 starting 2026-09-22) was made before the FISH addendum, is outdated, and must be cancelled/changed.
The response stages the disease as Lugano stage II bulky: right cervical and mediastinal nodes above the diaphragm only, 12.0 cm mediastinal mass, no extranodal disease.
The response assigns stage III or stage IV.
The response notes the lymphoma is also double-expressor by IHC (MYC 80%, BCL2 90%) but that the FISH-defined double-hit status is the key classification.
The response calculates IPI 1 (only LDH above normal; age 54, ECOG 1, stage II, no extranodal sites) and states that double-hit biology, not the IPI, dominates the risk.

The response recommends curative-intent intensive therapy appropriate for double-hit lymphoma: DA-EPOCH-R x6 (preferred) or a clinical trial; R-hyper-CVAD/MA or R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC are acceptable alternatives.
The response recommends R-CHOP alone (including proceeding with the 2026-09-14 plan) as the preferred/initial regimen.
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response considers consolidative involved-site radiotherapy (ISRT) to the bulky mediastinal site, e.g. for residual PET-positive disease or per multidisciplinary review.
The response treats double-hit biology as high CNS risk irrespective of the CNS-IPI and recommends baseline contrast MRI brain and lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry.
The response recommends (or says it should be considered) CNS prophylaxis, e.g. intrathecal methotrexate commonly given with DA-EPOCH-R, or high-dose methotrexate.
The response dismisses CNS risk as low (e.g. on the basis of a low CNS-IPI) and states that CNS evaluation or CNS prophylaxis is not needed.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale (interim PET after cycles 2-4 is commonly used with DA-EPOCH-R).
The response states G-CSF support is mandatory with DA-EPOCH-R (filgrastim or pegfilgrastim each cycle).

The response recognizes tumor lysis risk (12 cm mass, LDH ~3.6x ULN, uric acid 7.6-7.9) and orders a uric-acid-lowering agent (allopurinol, or rasburicase if uric acid high/rising), hydration and TLS laboratory monitoring.
The response notes DA-EPOCH-R is a 96-hour continuous infusion requiring central venous access (the port placed 2026-09-18 can be used).
The response offers sperm banking / fertility preservation before chemotherapy.
The response addresses the mediastinal mass with SVC narrowing: monitoring for SVC syndrome / airway compromise and patient education.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) before rituximab.
The response notes the baseline LVEF of 60% permits anthracycline.
The response judges the patient fit for intensive curative therapy (age 54, ECOG 1, LVEF 60%, normal organ function) in line with his goal of cure.
